newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares up, energy firms seen gaining.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares up, energy firms seen gaining.

text.p: Lithuanian shares edged up on Tuesday and dealers said that investors were showing an appetite for energy and electronics companies.
The Litin A index inched up 0.68 points to 2,605.33 and central market volume in equities was over 1.6 million litas.
Energy shares were in relative demand, with Lithuania Energy rising to 3.50 litas from 3.23 litas in trade worth over 455,000 litas.
Lithuania Gas slipped down to 2.35 litas from 2.36 litas and its shares turned over almost 280,000 litas.
"These shares could still pick up some momentum and go up...they have a lot of potential," said Tomas Andrejauskas of brokerage house Suprema.
"The government says it is going to privatise these firms and so investors want to get a piece of them now while the price is comparatively low," he said.
Dealers were also bullish on the electronics sector.
They said that Ekranas, which produces television components, looked set to rise.

Trade in its shares are currently suspended pending its shareholders' meeting but the company said on Tuesday that its net profit soared to 45.6 million litas after a loss of 13.8 million litas in 1995.
Electronics firm Vilniaus Vingis rose by almost ten percent to 5.50 litas in trade of 33,500 litas.
"Both of these companies look good and they are finding international partners and markets...so investors are looking at them," said one dealer.
Vilniaus Bank was another blue chip gainer on Tuesday, with its preferential shares rising to 1,600 litas from 1,570 litas. Its ordinary shares were unchanged at 259.90 litas.
The bank on Monday reported that its net profit had risen steeply to 24.4 million litas in 1996 versus 2.9 million litas the previous year.
Dealers were divided over the short-term impact which the results would have on its share price.
Some said it could only help but others said it was exactly what the market had expected and so the impact would be minimal.
Analysts also say the bank benefited from last year's banking crisis and predict that it will face stiffer competition this year as the sector as a whole recovers.
Over 316,000 litas worth of block trades were made and over 600,000 litas worth of T-bills changed hands.
